title: traffic-shaper-kv-coordination-sprint-67-log
content:
Weekly sync — sprint 67: Traffic Shaper & KV coordination

TL;DR
- Aim: reduce 99.9th latency tail during multi-tenant bursts by smoothing incoming request patterns at the ingress ("traffic-shaper") and improving KV cache coordination across kernels.
- This week we ran two small traffic-shaper experiments (stepped rate limiter + slot allocator) and a KV shadow-run to validate coordinated prefetch/evict heuristics.
- Observed: 7% reduction in p99.9 for short prompt workloads under synthetic spike, but increased median latency by ~3% in a few configs.
- Next actions: refine slot allocation thresholds, tune eviction hysteresis, run 24h canary under production-like traffic.

Attendees
- Maya Chen (owner, notes)
- Liam O'Connor (kernel/runtime)
- Priya Singh (cache/kv)
- Daniel Park (sre/infra)
- Sofia Alvarez (perf/eval)
- Andrew Holt (product liaison, 10m)

Summary of experiments
1) Stepped rate limiter (ingress)
   - Description: small stateful component at the routing layer that exposes per-tenant "slot" tokens. Instead of a flat QPS cap, it grants N concurrent generation slots and a short refill cadence (50ms). Designed to reduce burst-induced kernel saturation.
   - Run: A/B test for 6 hours against baseline using synthetic bursty traffic (mix of 32-64 token prompts).
   - Result: p99.9 reduced by 9% on average across GPUs during bursts. However, median latency rose by 2.4% for low-concurrency tenants due to slot contention. Tail improvement mainly came from fewer oversized batches queued at kernel scheduler.
   - Notes: eviction pressure lower during burst windows, implying fewer full KV evictions but more transient headroom fragmentation.

2) Slot allocator + soft-penalty fallback
   - Description: allocator that gives small guaranteed slots + soft-penalty for bursts beyond quota (degrade to smaller model-variant or slower throughput path).
   - Run: short smoke in staging with canary traffic mirroring top customers.
   - Result: reduced failed token generation (OOM/proxy-timeouts) by 60% during synthetic overload. User-visible output quality slightly impacted when on fallback; product okay with occasional fallback for a 5% user subset.
   - Notes: need product sign-off on fallback messaging and telemetry events for downstream analysis.

3) KV-shadow coordinated prefetch (prefetch shadow run)
   - Description: run new cooperative prefetch policy that shares approximate hot-key signals across kernels via lightweight Bloom sketch. Shadow traffic logged, no evictions applied.
   - Run: 48h shadow in production-read on a subset cluster.
   - Result: shadow logs show prefetch hit-rate improvement of ~11% for multi-turn chat sessions, but increased cross-kernel metadata chatter by +3% CPU. No memory anomalies observed.
   - Notes: false-positive rate in Bloom needs tuning; coordinate with infra to ensure metadata messages are rate-limited to control CPU impact.

Data and dashboards observed
- Key metrics (burst window): p50, p95, p99, p99.9 latency, kernel queue length, KV miss rate, eviction count, GPU utilization.
- p99.9: baseline 312ms -> traffic-shaper 289ms (7.4% improvement)
- p99: baseline 198ms -> traffic-shaper 190ms (4% improvement)
- median: baseline 72ms -> traffic-shaper 74ms (2.8% worse)
- KV miss rate: shadow policy expected hit-rate up 11% for tracked keys
- Eviction count: steady but patterns shifted (fewer large evictions, more small churn)

Operational observations / incidents
- During a stress run on day 2, a misconfiguration in the slot allocator caused double-allocation in one routing zone leading to transient overcommit and 10-minute elevated OOM rates. Root cause: race in allocator leases; fix deployed (synchronized lease write) and backfilled metrics.
- SRE request: add an emergency toggle (kill-switch) in the router to disable traffic-shaper per-zone. Implementation scheduled for next sprint.

Decisions taken
- Proceed to 24h canary with traffic-shaper + KV-coordination enabled on 12% of production reads (non-critical namespaces) after small fixes (lease sync, bloom tuning).
- Keep soft-fallback to smaller model-variant behind feature flag and only enable for non-SLA customers initially.
- Product will draft messaging for degraded model fallback; must be finalized before any wider rollout.

Open questions / risks
- Is the slight median latency regression acceptable vs tail improvements? Need metrics from real traffic A/B to measure user-perceived impact.
- Bloom sketch false positives: how aggressively can we tune size vs metadata bandwidth? Cost analysis pending.
- Cross-zone allocator fairness: current tests show zone-local fairness but inter-zone imbalance under geo-skewed traffic.

Action items (owners + ETA)
- Maya: consolidate shadow logs and create evaluation notebook for hot-key distributions (ETA: 2029-03-22)
- Priya: tune Bloom parameters and add per-kernel rate limit for metadata broadcast (ETA: 2029-03-24)
- Liam: patch allocator lease race + add unit test harness for multi-threaded lease handoff (ETA: 2029-03-21)
- Daniel: implement emergency toggle in router and add runbook for SRE (ETA: 2029-03-28)
- Sofia: run user-impact experiment framework to detect median-latency UX regressions (ETA: 2029-03-26)
- Product (Andrew): finalize fallback messaging and telemetry contract (ETA: 2029-03-25)

Notes to self / rough ideas
- Explore probabilistic slot allocation: give small fraction of slots stochastic extra capacity to reduce median regression while preserving tail smoothing.
- Consider hierarchical eviction: prefer cross-session tiny evictions rather than single-process full eviction. Might reduce headroom fragmentation.
- Evaluate KV-coord sketching alternatives (Count-Min vs Bloom vs TinyLRU signals).

Meeting transcript highlights (paraphrased)
- Liam: "Schedulers were queuing batches of 512 tokens during burst—those are expensive; smoothing reduced worst-case queue depth."
- Priya: "Bloom false positives show up as noisy prefetches for long-tail keys; we can gate by session score to limit blow-up."
- Daniel: "We need an operator kill-switch; when allocator misbehaves, it should be trivial to roll back without pipeline restarts."

Appendix / experiment config notes
- Traffic pattern: 2-phase burst (4s ramp -> 12s sustained -> 8s tail) repeated every 2 minutes, mixed request sizes (8/32/128 tokens).
- Shadow cohort: 3 nodes in us-west-2, read-only path, metadata logs to s3://rt-shadow/2029-03-18/
- Canary cohort planned: 12% traffic, exclude enterprise-SLA tenants, enable soft-fallback flag off by default.

If you want the raw dashboards / query links, ping me in #serving-runtime and I will share the grafana panels and the shadow logs.

-- Maya
